page: OVHcloud c3-128 is a compute-optimized server instance featuring 64 dedicated physical cores powered by an AMD EPYC x86_64 processor running at 2.3 GHz. The architecture allocates exactly one thread per core, ensuring dedicated execution resources without hyperthreading. It is configured with 128 GB of RAM, yielding a resource density of 2.0 GB per core. Local storage is provided by a 400 GB NVMe SSD, and the instance includes an 8 Gbps baseline network bandwidth alongside one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Benchmark data reveals a clear distinction between single-core and multi-core performance. While single-threaded tasks like gzip compression and Geekbench single-core execution register in the middle 50%, multi-threaded capabilities are highly competitive. The instance achieves top-tier status in stress-ng multi-core CPU performance, Passmark CPU physics, and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression. Memory bandwidth for small cached blocks also ranks in the top tier, though large-block uncached read and write operations drop to the strong category. This profile indicates a tradeoff where highly parallelized workloads benefit significantly, whereas single-threaded execution remains average.

Given the dedicated 64-core hardware profile and strong multi-core benchmarks, the c3-128 is suited for parallel computing tasks such as software compilation, ray tracing, and image processing, all of which scored in the top tier during testing. It also supports high-throughput database operations, demonstrated by a top-tier result of 137.31 million Redis SET operations per second. The qualitative cost efficiency of this instance lies in its high density of dedicated physical cores, making it a viable option for compute-bound workloads that do not require massive memory footprints.
description: OVHcloud c3-128 is a compute-optimized server featuring 64 dedicated physical cores on an AMD EPYC x86_64 processor running at 2.3 GHz with no hyperthreading. It is equipped with 128 GB of RAM, a 400 GB NVMe SSD, and an 8 Gbps baseline network interface. Benchmark results indicate top-tier multi-core CPU performance, software compilation speeds, and Redis SET throughput, alongside strong database and static web serving capabilities. Conversely, single-threaded performance and LLM text generation speeds fall into the average range. With a low memory-to-core ratio of 2.0 GB per core, this instance represents a tradeoff favoring dense parallel processing over memory-intensive operations. It is suited for multi-threaded workloads such as software compilation, ray tracing, image processing, and high-throughput caching.
